newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds ended a volatile day weaker but off their worst levels on Wednesday as institutions nibbled at yields which had been driven higher by earlier London-based selling.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the key R150 was pegged at a 15.10 percent yield compared with 15.04 percent on Monday after trading in a 14.97 to 15.13 percent range.
The market initially took heart from the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to hike interest rates which provided a fillip for gains on the U.S. Treasury bond market.
"But we saw some institutional selling and a bit of Reserve Bank funding below (15 percent) and the market ticked up again," a dealer said.
The move above 15 percent was followed by London-based selling shortly after noon which drove the R150 to its 15.13 percent intraday high.
"We saw some London selling... no particular reason, just screen trading and we moved up in sympathy," another trader said.
Some dealers said the market was discounting negative economic indicators which are due for release later in the week.

Preliminary August money supply is due on Friday, with economists predicting year-on-year M3 growth to increase to 15.7 percent from July's 14.69. Growth in private sector credit extension is seen slowing to 17.9 percent from 18.50 in July.
August trade figures are scheduled for release either on Friday or next week.
One trader noted that the market had closed on a bearish technical note after trading below its previous close and then closing above its previous finish.

"We have had a key day reversal which is a bit of a bearish signal," a dealer said, "but there are some institutions looking for a bit of paper around the 15.10 to 15.15 percent levels so we shouldn't go beyond there for now."
Trade on the currency market was more sedate as the rand clung to a narrow 4.5100 to 4.5140 range on the day.
"We've seen a bit of two-way trade but there is no real direction and no real interest," a dealer said.

The rand's failure to take advantage of the dollar's weakness against the mark after the Fed confounded market expectations of a rate hike was put down to mine violence at the weekend which claimed the lives of 21 people.
"The mine violence dented investor sentiment a bit," a dealer said.

At the finish, the rand was quoted at 4.5105/5155 on the dollar from 4.5100/510 on Monday, while against the crosses it was pegged at 7.0543/0666 on sterling from 7.0153/0253 on Tuesday and at 0.3342/3350 marks from 0.3350/3355.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 5.77 million rand worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 100.32 million on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 10.45 billion rand on Monday from 3.21 billion rand on Friday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged at 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage lower at 7.301 billion rand on Monday from 7.650 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
